scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for someone to lie to their boyfriend about seeing his ex-girlfriend at a party, especially when the lie seems to help the boyfriend move on faster. Let me break this down step by step. First, I need to understand the situation fully. The person in question is a college senior who started dating someone four months ago. The boyfriend had been dating another girl for his first two years in college, and they broke up because he suspected she was cheating. The person had a crush on the boyfriend since freshman year but knew he was in a relationship. Now, they're dating, but the boyfriend is still emotionally torn about the breakup. When he asked if the person saw his ex at a party, the person lied and said they saw her with other guys, which helped the boyfriend move on faster. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong to lie in this situation to help the boyfriend feel better and move on? I think the first thing to consider is the intention behind the lie. The person lied to help the boyfriend feel better and to give them a fresh start. That seems like a good intention. But lying itself is generally considered wrong because it breaks trust between people. Trust is essential in any relationship, and lying can damage that trust. On the other hand, the lie seems to have had a positive outcome. The boyfriend is happier now and has no regrets about the breakup. It helped him move on faster, which might have been beneficial for both of them. So, in this case, the lie led to a positive result. But I also need to think about the long-term consequences. If the boyfriend ever finds out that the person lied, it could damage the relationship severely. Trust is hard to rebuild once it's broken. Even if the lie had a positive outcome in the short term, the potential for long-term damage is significant. Another aspect to consider is the truth itself. The person didn't see the ex-girlfriend at the party, but they lied about it. By lying, they're altering the reality of the situation, which can lead to confusion and mistrust. It's important to be honest, even if the truth is difficult, because honesty builds a stronger foundation for the relationship. I also wonder about the alternative. What if the person had told the truth? Would the boyfriend have been upset, or would he have appreciated the honesty? It's possible that the truth might have caused more pain in the short term, but it would have been better for the relationship in the long run. Additionally, lying can create a cycle of deceit. Once you start lying to someone, it can become easier to lie again, even when it's unnecessary. This can lead to a breakdown in communication and a weaker relationship overall. In some cases, people might justify lying to protect someone's feelings, but in this situation, the lie is about a past relationship, not something that directly affects the current relationship. The boyfriend's happiness is important, but so is the integrity of the relationship built on trust. I also think about the concept of manipulation. By lying to make the boyfriend feel better, the person is manipulating the situation. Manipulation can be harmful because it takes away the other person's ability to make their own decisions based on truthful information. Moreover, lying can create internal conflict for the person who lied. They might feel guilty or anxious about keeping the lie a secret, which can affect their mental health and the relationship. In conclusion, while the lie in this situation seems to have had a positive outcome for the boyfriend, lying itself is generally considered wrong because it breaks trust and can lead to long-term damage in the relationship. It's better to be honest, even if it's difficult, to maintain trust and integrity in the relationship.
